findings.title: Non-atomic Phase-2 cutover: replaceDispatcher(idx) and setPrice(idx,10e6) are separate txs, so indices 1/2/3 mint-revert in the gap and stay stuck on an aborted broadcast
findings.description: The broadcast runs with --slow --skip-simulation, so replaceDispatcher(idx,uniboost), setPrice(idx,10e6) and setGrowthFactor(idx,2) inside _swapBurner are THREE separate on-chain txs. Between replaceDispatcher and setPrice, configs[idx] holds the new USDC-6dp Uniboost dispatcher but the OLD burner's 18-dp target-token price (live-read: 464.279e18 / 1.737e18 / 22876.13e18) and growth 1000. NFTMinterV2._executeMint would then require the minter to transferFrom `price` raw USDC units (~4.6e14..2.3e16 USDC) from the caller.
findings.impact: A mint on the affected index in that sub-window REVERTS (unaffordable transferFrom) — it FAILS SAFE (no under-charge, no mis-mint, no loss), but it is a live mint-DoS window. Under --slow the window is seconds-to-minutes; if the Ledger broadcast aborts (reject/gas/RPC) between the replace tx and the setPrice tx, that index is left persistently mint-reverting until the operator re-runs to completion. _swapBurner only checkpoints (_trackConfig) AFTER all three txs + post-asserts succeed, so resume correctly re-runs the whole block (idempotent: the second replaceDispatcher is a no-op because dispatcherToIndex[uniboost]==index).
findings.evidence: side-effects.json preconditionResults (live prices 464.279e18/1.737e18/22876.13e18, all astronomically unaffordable as 6-dp USDC); NFTMinterV2._executeMint charges configs.price of the dispatcher's primeToken (USDC). Fork preview confirms the intended end-state (10e6/2bps) once both txs land. Source confirmed: _trackConfig at line 435 fires only after all three mutations + post-asserts succeed (resume heals the gap).
findings.recommendation: Accept as fail-safe, OR make the window explicit and self-documenting: call setDispatcherDisabled(idx,true) before replaceDispatcher and re-enable after the reprice, or bundle replace+setPrice+setGrowthFactor for an index into a single owner action (multicall). At minimum document that a partial broadcast leaves the index mint-reverting (not cleanly disabled) until resume.

Known-issue #10 (admin trust) does NOT apply: this is a non-obvious operator footgun (Law 3 in-scope), not a reckless/malicious admin action. Fail-safe (no loss) → Low is honest.

findings.title: Phase-3 staker deploy and its 5 wiring steps share one checkpoint; a resume after the CREATE but before wiring permanently skips wiring, leaving an unwired staker that _verifyFinalState does not catch
findings.description: In _finalizeUniboost the staker block is guarded by `if (_isDeployed(stakerName)) return staker;`. Immediately after `new NFTStakerDepletion(...)` the script calls _trackDeployment (sets deployed=true) then _writeProgressFile() (persists deployed=true), and ONLY THEN performs the five wiring txs — s.setDispatcherHook(hook), UniboostMintDebtHook(hook).setRecipient(staker), s.setDepletionWindow(12), s.setPauser(PAUSER), Pauser.register(staker) — with NO per-step _trackConfig/checkpoint. Every other phase (1/2/4) checkpoints each config step individually; even the sibling donation block in this same function (line 464) is individually checkpointed, so the missing checkpoint is specific to the staker wiring.
findings.impact: If a broadcast lands the staker CREATE but not (all of) the subsequent wiring txs, a resume sees _isDeployed(stakerName)==true and RETURNS EARLY, permanently skipping the wiring. The result is a deployed-but-unwired staker: dispatcherHook==0 (cannot pull() -> accrued phUSD mint-debt is never realized to the staker), the Uniboost hook.recipient != staker (debt not directed to the pool), depletionWindow==0, and the staker not registered with the global Pauser (no pause coverage). _verifyFinalState asserts none of these, so the run still reports success and the misconfiguration is silent. This is the run-19 L-01 non-atomic-resume class, here specific to the Uniboost stakers.
findings.evidence: Source _finalizeUniboost confirmed at HEAD: _isDeployed early-return guard at line 472; _writeProgressFile() persists deployed=true at line 483 (right after the CREATE at line 478) BEFORE any wiring; the five wiring txs at lines 487-491 have no _trackConfig after them. _verifyFinalState (lines 621-641) omits all staker wiring. Contrast: _swapBurner (Phase 2) and the donation block (line 464) each checkpoint after their mutations.
findings.recommendation: Checkpoint each staker wiring step individually (mirror Phase 1/2/4), OR split the guard so wiring is re-attempted on resume even when the staker is already deployed, AND add the staker wiring invariants (dispatcherHook==hook, hook.recipient==staker, depletionWindowMonths==12, Pauser.registered(staker)) to _verifyFinalState.
findings.knownIssueReason: No match. Coarse resume-checkpoint granularity leaving a silently-unwired staker is not covered by any of the 11 known issues. Known-issue #10 (admin trust) does NOT apply: the documented core recovery path ('re-run to resume') actively cements a broken wiring — a competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised, so it is a non-obvious footgun (Law 3 in-scope), not admin malice/recklessness.

findings.title: _verifyFinalState is a partial post-condition: it omits the phUSD minter grants/revoke, donation config, hook.recipient, pooler-auth, staker wiring, and releaser/minter setup that the script performs
findings.description: _verifyFinalState asserts only configs(1/2/3) dispatcher+price+growth, configs(7) dispatcher, and RatchetNFTStaker.dispatcherHook. The script performs ~20 further safety-critical mutations that are NOT re-asserted: (a) the 5 phUSD.setMinter calls (4 new minters granted, OLD_RATCHET_HOOK revoked); (b) the 3 Uniboost setRecipient(BATCH_NFT_MINTER)+setDonationSplit(50); (c) the 3 Uniboost hook.setRecipient(staker); (d) MultiPooler.setPooler + the 3 setAuthorizedPooler(MultiPooler); (e) the 3 staker dispatcherHook/depletionWindow/Pauser registration; (f) NudgeRatchetDelayRelease.setMinter/setReleaser + newRatchetHook.setRecipient(RatchetNFTStaker); (g) OLD_RATCHET_HOOK phUSD-minter revoked.
findings.impact: Transparency/assurance gap: a silent mis-wire (including the UBC-02 skipped-wiring case, or a hand-edited progress file) completes with a 'verified' banner while leaving donations mis-routed, a hook unable to realize debt, a staker unprotected by the pauser, or an unintended residual phUSD minter. The steps do all run under guards in a clean full pass (confirmed by the fork preview), so this is assurance-surface, not a live defect on the happy path.
findings.evidence: Source _verifyFinalState confirmed (lines 621-641): asserts d1/d2/d3 dispatcher+price+growth, d7==newRatchet, and RatchetNFTStaker.dispatcherHook==newRatchetHook — nothing else. The full mutation set (Phases 1-5) is enumerated in side-effects.json stateWrites; fork preview shows all steps execute on a clean run.
findings.recommendation: Extend _verifyFinalState to positively assert the full wiring set — most importantly the 4 phUSD minter grants + the 1 revoke, each Uniboost hook.recipient==staker, each Uniboost recipient==BATCH_NFT_MINTER && donationSplit==50, and newRatchetHook.recipient==RatchetNFTStaker — so the post-condition actually proves the intended end state.
findings.knownIssueReason: No match. A verification-coverage / false-assurance gap (a 'verified' banner over an unverified end state) is not covered by any of the 11 known issues. It is not the external-vault OOS item (#9) — the gap is in the script's OWN post-condition logic, not external vault behavior. It is not admin-trust (#10). Non-obvious footgun (Law 3 in-scope); retained under Law 1 (recall beats tidiness).
